title: POC weekly sync - throughput optimization
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput test results and tune continuous batching, concurrency targets and queueing. Agreed next steps: run extended stress test at higher concurrency, adjust batching window and max queue size, Redwood to share updated benchmark spreadsheet and config snippets, schedule follow-up demo of dedicated capacity behavior.
topics: KV cache and prefix caching impacts
next_steps: Redwood to run 2-hour stress test at concurrency=48 and send logs + perf summary by 2025-03-07
BrightCart to provide production-like request distribution CSV by 2025-03-06
Redwood SE to share adjusted batching.conf and recommended max_queue_size by 2025-03-06

transcript:
Header: 2025-03-05 14:00 PST | Duration: ~38m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Patel, Evan Brooks (Redwood) - Maya Singh, Tom Rios, Samantha Cole (BrightCart)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — review last week's throughput numbers, dig into continuous batching effects, set concurrency targets, and outline next steps.
[00:22] Maya: Yep, thanks. We got the artifact you sent, the benchmark sheet, so we'll walk through the numbers.
[00:33] Priya: Great. Quick note — some naming in the sheet is old, I think we used "redwed dedicated" in one column, ignore that, it's Redwood Dedicated.
[00:47] Tom: Haha, cool. So baseline first: our prod-like payloads, median sequence ~120 tokens, tails up to 1024. We ran two passes: concurrency 16 and concurrency 32.
[01:05] Priya: Right, and just to recap for everyone, the runtime used continuous batching with a 10ms batching window and a max batch size of 64, and we had prefix/KV cash enabled — sorry I mean KV cache.
[01:26] Samantha: For us, the big thing is 95th percentile latency under normal load, and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:40] Jordan: Ok let's look at numbers, page 2 of the sheet — concurrency 16 gave about 2200 tok/s and p95 latency ~210ms; concurrency 32 improved throughput to 3500 tok/s but p95 jumped to ~420ms.
[02:05] Maya: The jump at 32 is surprising; we expected better linear scaling.
[02:12] Priya: Yeah so what we saw is queueing — at higher concurrency, batches often saturate the GPU kernel path and we accumulate head-of-line waits. Continuous batching reduces idle GPU, but if the max_queue_size is too small or if the batching window is short, you get more small batches which hurts eff.
[02:35] Tom: Can you explain "head-of-line" again?
[02:40] Priya: Sure — requests at the front of the queue block the backend while large KV cache lookups or long context runs finish, and subsequent arrivals sit waiting. If the scheduler doesn't preempt or re-balance by request size, the p95 degrades.
[02:58] Jordan: We also saw some variance depending on sequence length — longer tails amplify the head-of-line problem.
[03:07] Maya: Makes sense. Did you try changing batching window?
[03:11] Priya: Yes: 10ms vs 25ms vs 50ms. 25ms was the sweet spot for your mix — average batch size went up from 18 to 34, throughput improved ~20% and p95 dropped about 80ms vs 10ms. At 50ms we saw marginal additional throughput but higher latency for single-request flows.
[03:34] Samantha: So there's a tradeoff — increase batching window to help throughput, but hurt single-request tail latency. That's ok for async flows but not for interactive widgets.
[03:46] Tom: What about concurrency ceilings? We have SLAs for some endpoints 200ms p95.
[03:52] Priya: For your SLA endpoints, we recommend capping concurrency to 24 on hosted and using Dedicated for higher throughput. With concurrency 24 + batching window 25ms + max_batch_size 64, the p95 was ~195ms in our test.
[04:14] Maya: That's promising. How does autoscaling play in? We saw spikes last week up to conc 80 for a minute.
[04:21] Jordan: Autoscaling reacts but there's a 90s spin-up for new GPU capacity in Dedicated if it's cold; on Hosted we have burst nodes but they fall into lower-priority tiers. For short spikes, queueing + controlled reject/fallback is better than trying to spin new nodes immediately.
[04:39] Tom: Do you recommend queue/backpressure settings?
[04:43] Priya: Yes — set max_queue_size to 512 for your 50k RPS-ish flows, and enable server-side queuing with a 1.5s max wait for these non-interactive endpoints. For interactive, set max_queue_size 64 and lower wait to 250-350ms.
[05:05] Maya: Cool. Any kernel/quantization changes?
[05:09] Priya: We tested int8 quant on the model family and saw 1.6x speedup but +5-7% soft-regression on rare tokens; for many of your use cases that's acceptable. The kernel path for int8 also reduces memory pressure, which reduces KV cache eviction thrashing.
[05:31] Samantha: When you say KV cache eviction thrash, what does that look like?
[05:35] Priya: Essentially when the working set doesn't fit, we evict prefixes and re-populate causing higher compute. In the logs we saw lots of cache misses during long sessions which increased end-to-end latency. Larger batch sizes help amortize that, but memory profile matters.
[05:55] Tom: Any network effects? We have region splits and sometimes traffic routes cross regions.
[06:00] Jordan: If you route cross-region you add 30-60ms network tail; it's best to route to local region for latency-sensitive endpoints. Also the smart routing policy can failover to compatible model variants if Dedicated in a region is saturated.
[06:18] Maya: About the failover — does it keep the same tokenization and model fidelity? We can't afford quality regressions.
[06:24] Priya: We have model variants pinned to fidelity tiers; fallback prefers same family with similar sampling settings. We also validate via quick evals on canary traffic before broad failover.
[06:36] Samantha: Ok, demo request — can you show a scenario where Dedicated saturates and fallback kicks in?
[06:42] Jordan: Sure, we'll schedule that for the follow-up.
[06:46] Maya: Back to the numbers: the sheet shows p50 stable but p95 is where we care. Any config to reduce p95 without killing throughput?
[06:55] Priya: A few levers: increase batching window to 25ms, set request prioritization (SLA routes get smaller max_batch_size), and enable adaptive batching thresholds that shrink batch size when single-request latencies spike.
[07:15] Tom: Adaptive — is that available in hosted or only Dedicated?
[07:18] Priya: It's in both, but Dedicated gives you finer-grained kernel tuning and memory profile control. Hosted has safe defaults.
[07:26] Maya: The test had a weird blip at minute 18 where latency spiked for 60s. Any root cause?
[07:33] Priya: We correlated that to a background compaction job and a cross-tenant cache flush event on the node — some artifacts from the shared-hosted run. We recommend running the next stress in Dedicated or in an isolated host-pool to avoid that noise.
[07:51] Jordan: For reproducibility, we'll do the next run in an isolated Dedicated pool per Tom's earlier ask.
[07:58] Samantha: One ask — can you provide the exact benchmarking script and flags so we can re-run locally?
[08:03] Priya: Yes, I'll paste the script and the flags into the benchmark sheet; link will be in the follow-up email. Beware that some flags are internal names, one may show up as "batcher_v2" which is actually the continuous batching engine.
[08:20] Maya: On cost — at concurrency 32 with current config cost per 1k tokens was about $0.85; at 24 it was $1.02 due to longer tail? I might be reading that wrong.
[08:31] Jordan: I think those were swapped in column headers, there are a few transpositions in the spreadsheet — we'll correct and send clean numbers.
[08:40] Tom: OK. Anything on SLO enforcement and graceful degradation?
[08:44] Priya: We recommend route-level SLOs with automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants for non-critical endpoints, and immediate reject or queue for critical endpoints. Also enable tracing hooks to tie p95 regressions to prompt sets.
[09:03] Maya: Do you have an automated test we could run to validate p95 under our traffic distribution?
[09:08] Priya: Yes — we'll run the 2-hour stress with your CSV distribution and share the raw logs and a notebook to compute pxx.
[09:16] Samantha: Good. On the topic of quantization regressions, can we get a small eval suite?
[09:21] Priya: We'll add 50 representative prompts and run diff checks, send results.
[09:27] Jordan: Ok next area — queueing behavior during spikes. We recommend a hybrid approach: for bursts under 30s allow queueing up to 1.5s; for longer sustained loads prefer autoscale or degrade to a cheaper model variant.
[09:42] Tom: What about pre-warming? We could keep warm nodes at off-peak at low cost?
[09:47] Jordan: Dedicated supports pre-warmed pools and you can reserve a minimum of 2 nodes to reduce spin-up. That's part of the Dedicated contract.
[09:57] Maya: Quick question — you mentioned kernel selection earlier. Does Redwood pick kernels automatically per batch or per model?
[10:03] Priya: The runtime selects kernels per-model and per-batch characteristics. For example, short-context batches use attention kernel A, long-context uses kernel B which is slower but memory efficient. We tune selection thresholds in Dedicated for your workload.
[10:18] Samantha: Any logs we should be looking at specifically?
[10:21] Priya: Check batch size distribution, queue wait histogram, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and per-token generation CPU/GPU time. We'll include those charts.
[10:33] Tom: Do you have examples of config snippets?
[10:36] Priya: Yes, I'll drop the batching.conf snippet — sample: window_ms=25, max_batch_size=64, adaptive=true, max_queue_size=512, interactive_max_wait_ms=300.
[10:50] Maya: Can Redwood also simulate network latency to emulate cross-region calls?
[10:54] Jordan: We can add artificial latency in the test harness, yes.
[10:58] Samantha: Seems like we have enough to plan the next run.
[11:01] Priya: One more note — for long conversation sessions, increase KV cache capacity in Dedicated to avoid eviction thrash.
[11:10] Tom: Understood.
[11:13] Jordan: Alright let's summarize — Redwood runs 2-hour stress in Dedicated pool at concurrency 48, batching window 25ms, max_batch_size 64; BrightCart provides request CSV; Redwood shares updated sheet, configs, script, and small eval set.
[11:30] Maya: That sounds good. Also we'd like a short write-up on the quantization impact.
[11:34] Priya: We'll include that.
[11:36] Samantha: Thanks everyone.
[11:38] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with materials and calendar for the Dedicated demo.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present ("KV cash" instead of KV cache, "redwed" etc). References to shared artifacts: benchmark sheet (internal link), batching.conf snippet (to be shared), benchmarking script (to be shared).
